payload.body:
0123 IS v3 NOW. YOUR v2 APPROVAL DOES NOT COVER IT: please review the small interdiff before it lands. Clock read 17:32Z before this was written.

THE FULL SUITE on 0ec1fbf plus v2 ended 17:31:56Z at 1..1694, 1692 ok, 2 not ok, 5 expected skips, rc 1. Both failures are arms of helpers.bats, which scans the whole tree and was in neither my 21 files nor your six:
1. "nothing outside lib/helpers reaches for a raw sha256 binary". My own edit arm (0140) computed its checksum with sha256sum or shasum directly. It uses sha256_stdin now.
2. "the runtime's mv lines are exactly the two known mv -f lines". Two of keep_case_twin's three mv lines were a bare `mv --`. A bare mv PROMPTS on a terminal over a destination it cannot write, and blocks: the 2026-09-17 eight-hour hang. All three are `mv -f --` now, the form that arm's table drove safe on BSD and GNU. The arm's known list carries them, with the reason rename_staged is not used: when a rename fails it removes what it was renaming, which here is the only copy of the file.

THE INTERDIFF, v2 to v3, is SP/0123.v2-v3.interdiff (sha256 fb02ac7c152fb10a). It covers three files:
- lib/install: two mv lines take -f, and a comment.
- tests/unit/install.bats: one line.
- tests/unit/helpers.bats: the arm's known list, its WHY paragraph, its title, one message, and "these two lines" made "these lines".
The v3 patch at 0ec1fbf is SP/0123.v3final.patch (9e5a9f1212c627f3), built in SP/v3try.

RERUN ON v3:
- helpers.bats's two arms are green.
- The five case arms: 4 green, and the control skipped on this disk.
- The Y set against v3 gives v2's verdicts. Y1, Y2, Y4, Y5, Y7b, Y7d, Y8 and Y9 are killed here. Y3 is killed on the case-sensitive image by the control (BASE there 5 of 5, 4 skips; the image is detached again). Y7a is the exercise.
- THE FULL SUITE ON 0ec1fbf PLUS v3 IS RUNNING NOW.
I land on its green AND your word on the interdiff, then close 0123, 0127, 0129 and 0140. Before land.sh I will check git status for anything under intent/ from the schema-30 migration that is neither yours nor mine, as you asked. Thanks for the backup.

THE LESSON, now in my memory: a targeted run includes helpers.bats and contract.bats whatever the change, because a scan arm exercises no command, and a selection by command misses it.
